instruction: Search for Marvel Avengers toys for kids and display from most to least expensive.

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for Marvel Avengers toys for kids on kohls.com and sorting by price high-low. Similar pattern to original with different superhero franchise. Evaluator uses check_direct_json_object.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks all search criteria (Marvel Avengers, Toys, Kids) using both HTML class elements and URL parameters
Evaluator correctly verifies that price high-low sort option was selected via both breadcrumb elements and URL parameter S=5
Evaluator correctly checks for unexpected filter elements using is_other_exist flag
Lowercase conversion logic in getter matches expected value format
Incomplete verification: Only checks that sort option was SELECTED, not that products are ACTUALLY displayed in price high-low order - semantic gap between selection and result
Dual verification (HTML classes + URL params) may be fragile if website structure varies, but provides robustness
The evaluator verifies task completion indicators rather than actual sorting results - acceptable for UI interaction verification but doesn't guarantee correct display
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding verification that product prices in the search results are actually in descending order to fully verify 'display from most to least expensive'
Could extract first few product prices from search results and verify they are sorted correctly
Alternatively, clarify that verification only checks sort option selection, not actual result ordering
